A disputed boy goes to Abd bin Zam'a, the child belonging to the bed's owner, though Sauda screens herself; Suhaib, told to claim only his father, says he was kidnapped.
Abd bin Zam'a and Sa'd dispute a slave-girl's son; the Prophet gives the boy to Abd, as the son goes to the bed's owner, but tells Sauda to screen herself.
The Prophet gave the son of Zam'a's slave-girl to Abd bin Zam'a, born on his father's bed, though Sa'd claimed him for Utba, and told Sauda to veil from him.
Sa'd claims Zam'a's slave girl's son for his brother Utba; the Prophet gives him to Abd bin Zam'a, the child belonging to the bed, telling Sauda to screen herself.
Asking the Ansar whether any stranger was among them, the Prophet said the son of a people's sister belongs to them.
At the Conquest the Prophet rules Zam'a's slave-girl's son, claimed for Utba, is Abd bin Zam'a's brother, for the child belongs to the bed, but has Sauda veil from him.
Sa'd, first to shoot an arrow in Allah's cause, and Abu Bakra, who came over Ta'if's fort wall, report that knowingly claiming a false father denies one Paradise.
Zaid bin Haritha was called Zaid bin Muhammad until the verse came telling believers to call adopted sons by their fathers' names.
Everyone is a guardian responsible for his wards: the ruler for his people, a man for his family, a wife for her husband's house, a slave for his master's property.
Abdullah bin Amr is told his wife has a right over him, and everyone is a guardian: a man of his family, a wife of her husband's house and children.
After a Li'an case the child went to the wife alone, and over Zam'a's slave girl's son the Prophet ruled that the boy belongs to the bed's owner.
Zam'a's slave girl's disputed son went to the bed's owner, Sauda screening herself; knowingly claiming another man as father forbids Paradise; whoever denies his father is charged with disbelief.
The Prophet was delighted when Mujazziz, seeing only the uncovered feet of Zaid and Usama, said these feet belong to each other.
